name: Bismuth, thin film
equilibrium_context: Semimetal with three-dimensional Dirac electrons at the L point

driven_states.emergent_property: Helicity-dependent, instantaneous anomalous Hall conductivity. An effective Floquet model implies the emergence of a pair of double Weyl points through light-induced hybridization of occupied and unoccupied Dirac bands.
driven_states.source: Kanda, Murotani, Matsuda et al., arXiv:2301.06072 (2023), doi:10.48550/arXiv.2301.06072
driven_states.caveat: Preprint. No journal version traceable since January 2023 - this is itself an evidence signal, and the entry is weighted low accordingly. The double Weyl points are a model statement of the effective Floquet Hamiltonian, not a direct measurement; what is measured is only a helicity-dependent Hall conductivity, which, as in the Cd3As2 case from the same group, originates predominantly from resonant one-photon contributions.
driven_states.measured_quantity: THz Faraday rotation, real part of the Hall conductivity

gaps: Preprint without a journal version since 2023. verification_status remains pending.
